Build a Transfer Map

The Build a Map tool gives transfer course recommendations for a selected transfer institution with a specific undergraduate degree program at ASU. You can outline a transfer map by selecting almost any regionally accredited domestic institution and almost any ASU major.
You can favorite multiple transfer maps by selecting the heart within the transfer map search.
Building and saving a transfer map allows you to track your progress by adding details about where and when you plan to complete degree requirements.
Once you have been admitted to ASU, you will work with an Academic Advisor in your college to review the official major map for your catalog year.
The transfer map is a proactive planning tool; once you have started your academic career at ASU, the transfer map is replaced by the official degree audit (DARS).
Build a Transfer Map is only available for transfer institutions within the United States and for military Joint Service Transcripts.
You cannot build a transfer map for international coursework.
ASU only accepts credit from regionally accredited institutions.
Build a Transfer Map may not be compatible with institutions that have highly unique or experimental methods of instruction.
Students from institutions that fall into this scenario are encouraged to work with an Academic Advisor or transfer specialist.
You can indicate which courses you plan to complete elsewhere on your transfer map.
It is possible that ASU has not yet reviewed your course, or that the content of the course was determined to be insufficient or incompatible with the ASU requirement.
You can use additional helpful Transfer Guide tools such as Course Search and Submit Course for Evaluation to investigate specific transfer course equivalencies.
ASU does allow some courses to fulfill more than one requirement.
A single course may be used to satisfy only one core area.

When you use Build a Transfer Map to search for a major, you can 'favorite' that major by clicking on the heart icon. Keeping track of majors you might be interested in is helpful when you are first exploring degree options. You can compare how your transfer courses fulfill recommendations in various majors, and 'favorite' those transfer maps for future reference.
